title: Private VPC residency: provenance attestations, retention enforcement, and staged failback choreography
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers deploying Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem environments need deterministic proof that data never left permitted regions, that retention TTLs were enforced end-to-end at node and storage layers, and that automated regional failback (stage-by-stage) does not violate residency constraints. Current residency work surfaces separate attestations (location logs) and retention controls but lacks a single choreography for staged failback that: 1) embeds signed provenance for every data snapshot and request cache, 2) enforces retention TTLs at the orchestration level during failback, and 3) exports a tamper-evident evidence bundle consumable by auditors and Console.

Goal: Implement a staged failback choreography and evidence/export pipeline for Private/VPC deployments that provides signed provenance manifests, retention enforcement hooks in the orchestrator and node agents, and an automated evidence-package generator that uploads artifacts to the Compliance Console and produces an immutable audit bundle for customer download.
acceptance_criteria: Staged failback choreography implemented in the orchestrator that supports 3 stages (canary, cohort, full) and enforces region constraints per-stage
Provenance attestation: every snapshot and exported KV cache has a signed manifest (cosign-compatible) including node_id, region, timestamp, retention_ttl, and origin_request_id
Retention enforcement: orchestrator will refuse to rehydrate or replicate objects whose TTL has expired; node agent checks TTL before any cross-region transfer
Evidence export: generate a tamper-evident bundle (ZIP + manifest + chain-of-trust) and push to Console S3 bucket with checksum; download link appears in ticket UI
Automation: a single CLI command and Console button to simulate staged failback in a sandbox and produce the evidence bundle (no real data movement when simulating)
E2E tests: integration test that simulates canary failback and verifies attestations and retention checks are present and valid
work_items: Design choreography and state diagram for canary/cohort/full failback (in Confluence)
Extend node-agent to produce signed snapshot manifests and expose TTL metadata on object headers
Orchestrator policy: prevent replication to non-authorized regions and enforce TTL check before transfer
Evidence generator: package signer, bundle composer, Console upload API, and download link plumbing
Sandbox simulation mode for staged failback with synthetic metadata only
Add telemetry: metrics for blocked transfers due to TTL, attestations generated, and evidence bundle creation times
Docs: runbook for on-call and audit checklist for customers
updates: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: synced with PM and Legal to capture audit requirements. Agreed canonical fields for manifest: node_id, region, timestamp, retention_ttl, request_id, cosign_signature. Action: draft Confluence spec (MX link below).

2026-02-18 - Design review: decided on a 3-stage failback model (canary/cohort/full) to limit blast radius. PM requested retention policy must be authoritative and enforced by orchestrator rather than best-effort by nodes.

2026-02-22 - Engineering decision: use existing KMS integration + cosign signing model for manifests to avoid new crypto stacks. Node-agent to call local cosign helper to sign manifests before upload.
2026-02-25 - Prototype: node-agent now emits unsigned manifests in /var/tmp/residency-manifests; started cosign integration branch (github: redwood/re residency-attrs).

2026-02-28 - Security review kickoff: submitted architecture diagram and threat model to Security (ticket SEC-2142). Security requested a short retention of signing keys in memory and rotation guidance.
2026-03-01 - Integrated retention checks in orchestrator policy engine PR opened (github: redwood/orch#732). Coverage: refusal path for expired TTL; next: evidence composer work
risks: Edge-case: customers with strict air-gapped environments may reject external signature verification; need on-prem KMS flow tested
Operational: generating evidence bundles for large clusters may be IO-intensive and slow; need throttling and incremental bundle streaming
Complexity: choreography increases state machine surface area which may complicate rollback and retry semantics
Compliance: legal may require longer immutable retention for evidence exports in certain jurisdictions
qa_notes: Use sandbox mode to run failure scenarios without moving customer data
Validate cosign signatures with the public key bundle in Console before marking evidence as valid
Load-test evidence export on a 50-node cluster in staging to measure time and IO
next_steps: Merge orchestrator TTL enforcement PR and run e2e in staging
Finalize cosign key rotation guide with Security and Ops
Implement evidence composer and Console upload endpoint
Schedule customer pilot with two enterprise customers who requested region failback assurance
